items.title: 2.2.1 Intersection of a Linear Function and Coordinate Axes (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Is sabaq mein hum dekhenge ke ek seedhi line (linear function ka graph) \(x\)-axis aur \(y\)-axis ko kahan kaat'ti hai. Yeh graph ki sab se buniyadi skill hai; aage do lines aur line-parabola wale sawalon mein bhi yahi kaam baar baar aayega.

Kitab yaad dilati hai: linear function woh function hai jis mein variable ki sab se bari power ek ho (jaise \(y = 2x + 6\); yahan \(x\) ki power 1 hai, \(x^{2}\) nahin hai). Aur coordinate axes se muraad Cartesian coordinate system ke \(x\)-axis aur \(y\)-axis hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Linear function ki aam shakal \(y = mx + c\) hai, aur is ka graph hamesha ek seedhi line hota hai. Seedhi line kheenchne ke liye do points kaafi hain, lekin teesra point lena achhi aadat hai: agar teeno ek seedh mein na aayein to foran pata chal jata hai ke hisaab mein ghalti hai.
Ab asal baat: \(x\)-axis ke har point par \(y = 0\) hota hai (wahan aap na upar gaye na neeche). Aur \(y\)-axis ke har point par \(x = 0\) hota hai (wahan aap na daayen gaye na baayen). Is liye:
line \(x\)-axis ko wahan milti hai jahan \(y = 0\) ho; is point ko \(x\)-intercept kehte hain;
line \(y\)-axis ko wahan milti hai jahan \(x = 0\) ho; is point ko \(y\)-intercept kehte hain.
Intercept ka matlab hai woh jagah jahan line axis ko "kaat'ti" hai.
Ab kitab ki misaal dekhte hain. Kitab graph bana kar jawab parhti hai; hum saath saath algebra se tasdeeq bhi karenge.

blocks.title: Example 7
blocks.problem: Find the points of intersection of a linear function \(y = 2x + 6\) and coordinate axes.
steps:
Given: linear function \(y = 2x + 6\).
To find: woh points jahan is ki line \(x\)-axis aur \(y\)-axis ko milti hai.
Method: sab se pehle hum dekhte hain ke humein kya chahiye: do points, ek har axis par. Kitab ka tareeqa: table of values banao, points plot karo, line kheencho, aur dekho line axes ko kahan kaat'ti hai. Phir \(y = 0\) aur \(x = 0\) rakh kar check karenge.

Step 1: Table of values banayein
\(x = -1, 0, 1\) chun kar \(y\) nikaalein:
\[x = -1:\ y = 2(-1) + 6 = 4\]
\[x = 0:\ y = 2(0) + 6 = 6\]
\[x = 1:\ y = 2(1) + 6 = 8\]
Kyun: har \(x\) ki value humein line ka ek point \((x, y)\) deti hai. Chhoti values (\(-1, 0, 1\)) is liye li hain ke hisaab aasan rahe aur ghalti ka imkaan kam ho. Dhyan dein: \(2(-1) = -2\), aur \(-2 + 6 = 4\); minus ka sign yahan aksar choot jata hai.

Step 2: Points plot kar ke line kheenchein
\((-1, 4)\), \((0, 6)\) aur \((1, 8)\) graph par lagayein aur ruler se jor dein. Line ko dono taraf aage tak barhayein (neeche table aur graph dekhiye).
Kyun: linear function ka graph seedhi line hai. Teeno points ek seedh mein aa rahe hain, is ka matlab hai table mein koi ghalti nahin. Line ko barhana zaroori hai, warna woh \(x\)-axis tak pahunchegi hi nahin aur intercept nazar nahin aayega.

Step 3: Axes par points parhein
Line \(x\)-axis ko \((-3, 0)\) par aur \(y\)-axis ko \((0, 6)\) par kaat'ti hai.
Kyun: \(x\)-axis par har point ka \(y = 0\) hota hai, aur \(y\)-axis par har point ka \(x = 0\). Is liye axis wale points ka ek coordinate hamesha zero hoga.

Tasdeeq:
Ab algebra se check karte hain ke graph se parha hua jawab sahi hai.
\(y = 0\) rakhein:
\[0 = 2x + 6\]
\[2x = -6 \Rightarrow x = -3\]
\(x = 0\) rakhein:
\[y = 2(0) + 6 = 6\]
Dono graph se mil gaye: \((-3, 0)\) aur \((0, 6)\). Jawab pakka hai.
blocks.answer: Line \(y = 2x + 6\) \(x\)-axis ko \((-3, 0)\) par aur \(y\)-axis ko \((0, 6)\) par milti hai.

blocks.alt: Graph of the line y = 2x + 6 on axes marked from minus 4 to 4 (x) and minus 4 to 8 (y). The plotted points are (minus 1, 4), (0, 6) and (1, 8). The line cuts the x-axis at (minus 3, 0) and the y-axis at (0, 6).
blocks.caption: Figure: graph of y = 2x + 6 meeting the axes at (−3, 0) and (0, 6) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Is tarah graph se saaf hai ke \((-3, 0)\) aur \((0, 6)\) woh points hain jahan \(y = 2x + 6\) coordinate axes ko kaat'ti hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ab ek aur line par yahi kaam khud kar ke dekhiye (yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin): \(y = -3x + 6\).
\(y = 0\): \(0 = -3x + 6 \Rightarrow 3x = 6 \Rightarrow x = 2\), yani \(x\)-intercept \((2, 0)\).
\(x = 0\): \(y = 6\), yani \(y\)-intercept \((0, 6)\).
Table se bhi dekh lein: \(x = 1\) par \(y = 3\); points \((0, 6), (1, 3), (2, 0)\) ek seedh mein hain. Yeh line neeche ki taraf jati hai kyun ke \(m = -3\) negative hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(y = mx + c\) mein \(x = 0\) rakhein to kya milta hai? (Jawab: \(y = c\). Yani \(y\)-intercept hamesha \((0, c)\) hota hai, bina hisaab ke parh sakte hain. \(y = 2x + 6\) mein \(c = 6\), is liye \((0, 6)\).) Aur kya line \(y = 5\) \(x\)-axis ko kahin kaat'ti hai? (Nahin: yeh \(x\)-axis ke parallel hai.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Linear function \(y = mx + c\) ka graph seedhi line hai.
2. \(x\)-intercept ke liye \(y = 0\) rakhein; \(y\)-intercept ke liye \(x = 0\) rakhein.
3. \(y = mx + c\) ka \(y\)-intercept hamesha \((0, c)\) hai.
4. Do points se line ban jati hai; teesra point check ke liye.
5. Graph se parha hua jawab algebra se zaroor check karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Coordinates ulat dena: \(y = 2x + 6\) ka \(x\)-intercept \((-3, 0)\) hai, \((0, -3)\) nahin. Yaad rakhein: \(x\)-axis wale point mein \(y\) zero hota hai.
2. \(0 = 2x + 6\) hal karte hue sign ki ghalti: \(x = -3\) aata hai, \(3\) nahin. Six ko doosri taraf le jaayein to \(-6\) banta hai.
3. Line ko sirf plot kiye hue points tak rokna: use dono taraf itna barhayein ke dono axes ko kaat de.
4. Ghalat scale: dono axes par har khaane ki value saaf likhein, warna point ghalat jagah lagega.
